Healthy Living Overland Park Elementary Norovirus Outbreak Ends After 97 Illnesses as Johnson County Warns the True Count Is Higher Published Oct 22, 2026 10:55 PM EDT By Dorothy Brooks OLI SCARFF | AFP via Getty Images Share on Twitter Share on Facebook Share on WhatsApp Johnson County health officials have declared a norovirus outbreak at Bentwood Elementary School in south Overland Park after 97 people fell ill, KCTV5 reported on October 21. Of those, 95 cases were among students and staff inside the school, and two were among family members outside it, Johnson County Department of Health and Environment Director Charlie Hunt said. Hunt said the true number is likely higher because norovirus is so contagious. Mild cases often go unreported, and some families likely cared for sick children at home without contacting anyone. The school sits near 129th Street and Quivira Road but belongs to the Olathe School District. For Kansas City-area parents, the episode is an early reminder that stomach bugs spread fast in classrooms, even as flu cases begin to rise. Inside the Bentwood Timeline The district said absences involving similar symptoms first appeared on Thursday, October 8. Students were out the next day for a scheduled professional development day, and crews deep-cleaned the building that weekend. On Monday, October 12, absences reached 10%, the threshold that triggers contact with the Johnson County Department of Health and Environment. The department then began determining whether the illnesses met the definition of an outbreak, while custodians deep-cleaned and disinfected high-touch surfaces and high-traffic areas daily. The building was cleaned again during scheduled days off later that week. Two people with symptoms tested positive for norovirus. Based on those results and 82 other people who reported similar symptoms between October 8 and 14, the county declared an outbreak. Health officials said the cases were epidemiologically linked, meaning people had similar symptoms at the same time in the same setting. The total later grew to 97. The county and district notified Bentwood families on October 19. Parent Samantha Pedraza said she first heard about the outbreak through parent text messages and apps before that notice arrived, and she knows of families where several children or parents got sick. "I was surprised we had such a heavy amount of it so quickly," she said. By Wednesday, October 21, only one student was absent with similar symptoms, according to the district. Officials have not publicly identified a source. Norovirus outbreaks in schools often spread from person to person and through contaminated surfaces, which can make a single starting point hard to pin down. Why the Virus Moves So Fast Through Classrooms Norovirus infects the digestive tract and causes nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. According to the CDC, it spreads through direct contact with sick people, contaminated food or water and contaminated surfaces. Dr. Dana Hawkinson, medical director of infection prevention and control at the University of Kansas Health System, said the virus easily contaminates shared spaces, and its tiny particles make it hard to know when you have touched them. His advice for families was direct: "Do adequate hand washing, especially after using the restroom." Hawkinson stressed soap and water, and Pedraza said she has emphasized handwashing with her child because hand sanitizer does not work well against norovirus. She said the school nurse posted handwashing signs for students. Disinfecting doorknobs, counters, and phones also helps. Hawkinson said sick children should stay home for at least 48 hours and until they are better and can control their bowel movements. Sick adults should stay home from work for the same reason. Hunt noted there is no vaccine for norovirus, and antibiotics do not work against it because it is a virus. Johnson County typically sees three to five norovirus outbreaks a year, ranging from a handful of cases to a couple dozen, he said. Bentwood was on the larger side, but not record-setting. Nationally, about 2,500 norovirus outbreaks are reported each year, according to the CDC's outbreak data, a figure Hunt said is also likely an undercount. Families Most at Risk and When to Seek Care Most people recover in two to three days without specific treatment. The main danger is dehydration from fluid loss, which hits hardest in the very young, older adults and people with weakened immune systems or chronic illness, Hawkinson said. Warning signs of dehydration include urinating very little, a dry mouth, and dizziness when standing. In young children, crying with few or no tears and unusual sleepiness are also red flags. Parents should call a pediatrician if a child cannot keep fluids down and seek urgent care for signs of severe dehydration or a child who is hard to wake. Immunity after infection fades. Hawkinson said people likely have some protection for the next two to three weeks but can be infected again months later, so a household that already had the virus should not drop its guard for the whole season. For working parents, the practical cost is missed school and work. Keeping a child home for the full 48 hours can be hard, but sending children back early helps the virus keep spreading. MedicalDaily will watch for new school or child-care clusters in Johnson County as winter approaches. The Bentwood outbreak is over, but steady handwashing remains a household's strongest defense. Johnson County confirmed a norovirus outbreak that sickened 97 people, including 95 students and staff, and has since declared it over. Was the source found? Officials have not publicly identified a source. The illnesses were linked by timing, setting, and symptoms, with two lab-confirmed cases. What are the symptoms of norovirus? Nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea, which usually last two to three days. Does hand sanitizer stop norovirus? Not reliably. Washing hands with soap and water and disinfecting high-touch surfaces work better. When can a sick child return to school? A University of Kansas Health System expert advised waiting at least 48 hours and until the child has recovered. Who should seek medical care? Anyone showing signs of dehydration, especially young children, older adults, and people with weakened immune systems. news.content_title: Nearly 100 cases of norovirus reported at elementary school
news.content: A Kansas elementary school suffered an outbreak of norovirus that impacted nearly 100 people, health officials said. The outbreak at Bentwood Elementary School in Olathe, Kansas, began in early October and spread to 95 cases of norovirus among students and staff and two cases among family members, officials with the Johnson County Department of Health and Environment and Olathe Public Schools told ABC News in a statement Thursday. Two of the cases were confirmed through laboratory testing, with the remaining cases being "epidemiologically linked, meaning individuals experienced similar symptoms around the same time and in the same setting," officials said. Google Maps Street View - PHOTO: Bentwood Elementary School in Overland Park, Kansas. Norovirus is a highly contagious virus that is the most common cause of viral gastroenteritis, an inflammation of the inside lining of the gastrointestinal tract. According to school and county health officials, people impacted by the outbreak at Bentwood Elementary experienced symptoms including vomiting, diarrhea, nausea and stomach pain. No hospitalizations were reported, and no new cases have been reported since Oct. 13, officials said. "Throughout the outbreak, JCDHE worked closely with school officials to monitor illnesses, provide public health guidance and help prevent further spread," the school district and health department said in a joint statement. "Although the outbreak is considered over, JCDHE and the Olathe Public Schools will continue to monitor the situation and work together to help protect the health of students, staff and families." Norovirus is the leading cause of foodborne illness in the U.S., causing 58% of those illnesses each year, according to the CDC. Annually, around 21 million Americans are diagnosed with norovirus. The most common symptoms for norovirus are nausea, vomiting, stomach pain and diarrhea. Patients can also experience fever, headaches and body aches. Norovirus is incredibly contagious and frequently reported in school settings, where children interact in close quarters. What to know about the symptoms and treatment of norovirus Most people recover within 1 to 3 days but can still spread the virus for a few days after. The most effective way to prevent the spread of norovirus is hand washing with soap and water, according to the CDC. Hand sanitizer does not kill norovirus. news.content_original: A Kansas elementary school suffered an outbreak of norovirus that impacted nearly 100 people, health officials said. The outbreak at Bentwood Elementary School in Olathe, Kansas, began in early October and spread to 95 cases of norovirus among students and staff and two cases among family members, officials with the Johnson County Department of Health and Environment and Olathe Public Schools told ABC News in a statement Thursday. Two of the cases were confirmed through laboratory testing, with the remaining cases being "epidemiologically linked, meaning individuals experienced similar symptoms around the same time and in the same setting," officials said. Google Maps Street View - PHOTO: Bentwood Elementary School in Overland Park, Kansas. Norovirus is a highly contagious virus that is the most common cause of viral gastroenteritis, an inflammation of the inside lining of the gastrointestinal tract. According to school and county health officials, people impacted by the outbreak at Bentwood Elementary experienced symptoms including vomiting, diarrhea, nausea and stomach pain. No hospitalizations were reported, and no new cases have been reported since Oct. 13, officials said. "Throughout the outbreak, JCDHE worked closely with school officials to monitor illnesses, provide public health guidance and help prevent further spread," the school district and health department said in a joint statement. "Although the outbreak is considered over, JCDHE and the Olathe Public Schools will continue to monitor the situation and work together to help protect the health of students, staff and families." Norovirus is the leading cause of foodborne illness in the U.S., causing 58% of those illnesses each year, according to the CDC. Annually, around 21 million Americans are diagnosed with norovirus. The most common symptoms for norovirus are nausea, vomiting, stomach pain and diarrhea. Patients can also experience fever, headaches and body aches. Norovirus is incredibly contagious and frequently reported in school settings, where children interact in close quarters. What to know about the symptoms and treatment of norovirus Most people recover within 1 to 3 days but can still spread the virus for a few days after. The most effective way to prevent the spread of norovirus is hand washing with soap and water, according to the CDC. Hand sanitizer does not kill norovirus. Current CDC data show that cases of norovirus are at medium levels nationally, without significant spikes. news.content: Norovirus Treatment Market Report 2026 Market Outlook Supported By A Forecast 10.6% CAGR An in-depth look at the norovirus treatment market reveals significant growth potential fueled by evolving healthcare needs and technological advancements. This overview explores the current market size, growth drivers, key players, emerging trends, and essential market segments shaping the future of norovirus care. Norovirus Treatment Market Size and Growth Forecast The norovirus treatment market has experienced rapid expansion in recent years. From a valuation of $1.94 billion in 2025, it is anticipated to rise to $2.15 billion in 2026, reflecting a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 10.9%. This historical growth phase has been influenced by low awareness about norovirus management, a strong dependence on hospital treatments, inadequate homecare infrastructure, lack of consistent symptom management protocols, and limited use of probiotics and zinc supplements. Download a free sample of the norovirus treatment market report: https://thebusinessresearchcompany.com/sample_request?id=15507317&type=smp&name=Norovirus%20Treatment%20Market%20Report%202026&utm_source=OpenPR&utm_medium=Paid&utm_campaign=Oct_PR Looking ahead, the market is expected to maintain its brisk pace, reaching $3.22 billion by 2030 with a CAGR of 10.6%. This anticipated surge is driven by factors such as increased demand for oral rehydration solutions, expanded homecare services and telemedicine adoption, heightened focus on pediatric and elderly patient groups, advancements in targeted supportive care therapies, greater healthcare spending, and intensified awareness campaigns. Key trends projected to shape this period include wider acceptance of oral rehydration therapies, growing intravenous fluid use for severe cases, rise in remote and home-based treatment options, broader utilization of anti-diarrheal and symptom management medications, and specialized care targeting vulnerable age groups. Prominent Players Leading the Norovirus Treatment Market The norovirus treatment sector is supported by numerous influential companies, including Abbott Laboratories, Reckitt Benckiser Group plc, Nestlé Health Science, Otsuka Pharmaceutical Co. Ltd., Dr. Reddy's Laboratories Ltd., Cipla Limited, Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd., Aurobindo Pharma Limited, Lupin Limited, Mylan (Viatris Inc.), Perrigo Company plc, Haleon plc, Church & Dwight* Co. Braun Melsungen AG, Hikma Pharmaceuticals PLC, Torrent Pharmaceuticals Ltd., Alkem Laboratories Ltd., Zydus Lifesciences Ltd., Glenmark Pharmaceuticals Ltd., Pfizer Healthcare India Pvt. Ltd., Mead Johnson Nutrition (Reckitt), Danone Nutricia, Amneal Pharmaceuticals Inc., and Ajanta Pharma Ltd. View the full norovirus treatment market report: https://www.thebusinessresearchcompany.com/report/norovirus-treatment-global-market-report?utm_source=OpenPR&utm_medium=Paid&utm_campaign=Oct_PR In a noteworthy development in March 2024, Kenvue Inc., a US-based consumer healthcare firm, teamed up with the Association of Physicians of India (API) to boost public health awareness and preventive care efforts. This collaboration focuses on enhancing clinical guidelines related to hydration and energy management for hospitalized patients without diarrheal conditions, relying on evidence-based recommendations jointly developed with API, a professional body representing internal medicine practitioners in India. Emerging Innovations and the Path Ahead in Norovirus Treatment Industry leaders are increasingly channeling efforts into innovative solutions like advanced mRNA vaccines, which promise to accelerate targeted immunizations, boost protection against severe norovirus infections, and reduce the global disease burden. These next-generation vaccines employ engineered messenger RNA to instruct cells to produce specific proteins, eliciting strong immune responses with improved stability, efficiency, and adaptability against infectious diseases. A prime example took place in October 2024 when Moderna Inc., a US biotechnology company, collaborated with the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) to launch the world's first Phase 3 trial of an mRNA norovirus vaccine (mRNA-1403) in the United Kingdom. This vaccine aims to stimulate a robust immune reaction by prompting the body to generate viral proteins without using live virus particles. news.content: News Issues Wellness Beauty Pharma KOREAN SEARCH Search Health Chosun Norovirus Risk Extends Beyond Oysters, with Leafy Greens Linked to 32% of Foodborne Cases by Kim Bo Mi Updated 2026/10/27 13:06 Norovirus can also be contracted through vegetables. /AI-generated photo Norovirus infections surge from November, when the weather turns cold. Oysters are a 대표적인 food ingredient that raises the risk of infection, but people can also contract norovirus through vegetables. Norovirus can survive even at minus 20°C. It can enter the body through contaminated ingredients, including seafood as well as fruits and vegetables. In particular, vegetables stored in the refrigerator should not be eaten without washing them. An investigation by the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, CDC, into foods linked to norovirus outbreaks from 1998 to 2008 found that leafy greens accounted for the highest proportion, at 32%. Vegetables should be washed thoroughly before eating. /AI-generated photo When washing vegetables, soak them in water first and then rinse them thoroughly under running water. The MFDS analyzed the effectiveness of different washing methods in removing norovirus from lettuce and perilla leaves that had been artificially contaminated with the virus. The analysis found that soaking them in water for 2 minutes and then washing them under running water for 30 seconds removed 87.5% and 94.8% of the norovirus, respectively. When storing food, keep it in a separate container to prevent cross-contamination. Fruits and vegetables stored in the refrigerator after washing should also be washed again before eating. Food should preferably be heated to at least 85°C for 1 minute or longer before eating. Knives and cutting boards should be disinfected, and using separate cooking utensils for vegetables, meat and fish can lower the risk of infection. Wash your hands with soap under running water for at least 30 seconds before handling food. People infected with norovirus should be cautious about dehydration. Drinking boiled water with sugar and salt can help. /AI-generated photo People infected with norovirus develop symptoms of vomiting and diarrhea within 1 to 2 days. Abdominal pain, chills, fever, nausea and muscle aches can also occur. Most people recover naturally after 2 to 3 days, but caution is needed because dehydration can occur. If dehydration is severe, treatment involving intravenous fluid administration may be considered. When symptoms occur, drink plenty of fluids through sports drinks without caffeine or alcohol. The Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency said it is also helpful to drink boiled water mixed with four tablespoons of sugar and one tablespoon of salt per 1 L. Do not take antidiarrheal or antiemetic medication on your own without a doctor's examination. Once diarrhea symptoms improve, eat small amounts of thin rice porridge or rice gruel. If a family member has norovirus, separate the person's living space from the rest of the household. Disinfect items the patient has touched or used with a mixture of bleach and water in a ratio of 1 to 50. Clothes should preferably be sanitized by washing them at 70°C or higher. To be safe, the patient should not prepare food for 3 days after recovering. This article has been translated AI. by Kim Bo Mi View All Articles Copyright © Health Chosun. news.content: Topics Business & Management Carpet Facility Management Hard Floors Health & Safety Infection Control Products Restrooms Technology & Trends Training Follow CMM Facebook X LinkedIn Get Your CMM Magazine Subscription Sign up for the CMM Newsletter Advertise with Us Join ISSA News Magazine Resources Certifications / Standards Safer Choices Product Innovation Showcase Sponsored Content Education Videos Industry Research On-Demand Webinars Follow CMM Facebook X LinkedIn Get Your CMM Magazine Subscription Sign up for the CMM Newsletter Advertise with Us Join ISSA Events ISSA Show Industry Events Upcoming Webinars Follow CMM Facebook X LinkedIn Get Your CMM Magazine Subscription Sign up for the CMM Newsletter Advertise with Us Join ISSA ISSA Media Follow CMM Facebook X LinkedIn Get Your CMM Magazine Subscription Sign up for the CMM Newsletter Advertise with Us Join ISSA Contact Subscribe ADVERTISE Nearly 100 Cases of Norovirus Reported at One Kansas School Norovirus cases are at medium levels nationally October 27, 2026 A Kansas elementary school experienced a norovirus outbreak that affected nearly 100 people, Johnson County Health officials said. The outbreak at Bentwood Elementary School in Olathe, Kansas, began in early October and spread to 95 cases among students and staff and two among family members in the Kansas City metropolitan area. Two of the cases were confirmed through laboratory testing, and the remaining cases were “epidemiologically linked, meaning individuals experienced similar symptoms around the same time and in the same setting,” officials said. Norovirus is the leading cause of vomiting, diarrhea and foodborne illness in the United States, and people of all ages can get infected and sick with norovirus, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. According to school and county health officials, people impacted by the outbreak at Bentwood Elementary experienced symptoms including vomiting, diarrhea, nausea and stomach pain. Officials said no hospitalizations were reported, and no new cases have been reported since Oct. 13. Throughout the outbreak, the local health department has worked closely with school officials to monitor illnesses, provide public health guidance and help prevent further spread. While the outbreak is considered over, local teams will continue to monitor the situation. Annually, around 21 million Americans are diagnosed with norovirus. The virus is incredibly contagious and frequently reported in school settings, where children interact in close quarters. The CDC said the most effective way to prevent norovirus spread is washing hands with soap and water. Hand sanitizer does not kill norovirus. Current CDC data shows that norovirus cases are at medium levels nationally, without significant spikes. Tags U.S. Green Building Council Streamlines Zero Waste Certification October 27, 2026 Last week, the U.S. Green Building Council (USGBC) launched TRUE v2—the next iteration of the TRUE (Total Resource Use and Efficiency) zero waste certification program. The new version of the rating system emphasizes zero waste impacts and global applicability, and it helps organizations advance their decarbonization, business transformation and circularity goals. For more than 10 years, TRUE has reshaped waste operations for organizations, companies and small businesses, with over 680 certified projects totaling 272 million square feet and diverting 8.9 million tons of waste from landfills. The streamlined rating system collects, measures, benchmarks and verifies sustainability performance. Updates to the TRUE v2 rating system include: Rebalanced credit structure to support projects starting their zero-waste journey while also rewarding high performers. Improved global usability with clearer, internationally applicable language and approaches. Greater rewards for higher-impact and harder-to-achieve actions. TRUE v2 comes as more organizations seek clarity on zero waste roadmaps, with waste volumes rising, landfill capacity tightening, and disposal costs escalating. The Global Waste Management Outlook 2024 projects that the direct cost of waste management could double by 2050, and the Environmental Research and Education Foundation found that commercial waste disposal costs in the U.S. have grown by 15-30% since 2016. TRUE v2 was developed with USGBC members and stakeholders, including the TRUE Advisory Council, and informed by global public consultation from zero waste practitioners. Registration for TRUE v2 is now open on the Arc platform for projects interested in advancing their zero waste goals and pursuing certification. news.content: Kansas elementary school's norovirus outbreak sickened 97, and sanitizer won't stop it Nearly 100 people connected to a Kansas elementary school fell ill with norovirus, a reminder of how fast stomach illnesses can spread in schools — and why soap-and-water handwashing matters more than sanitizer for this virus. Here's what to know According to ABC News, Bentwood Elementary School in Olathe, Kansas, logged 95 illnesses among students and staff, plus two more among family members. Health officials and the school district said no one was hospitalized, and as of Thursday, they had not reported any additional cases since Oct. 13. Lab testing confirmed two illnesses. The rest were treated as epidemiologically linked, meaning people in the same setting developed similar symptoms at roughly the same time. Reported symptoms included vomiting, diarrhea, nausea, and stomach pain. These are classic signs of norovirus, a highly contagious virus that causes viral gastroenteritis, or inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract lining. More background The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention identifies norovirus as the most common cause of viral gastroenteritis, and schools can be ideal places for it to spread because children spend hours in close quarters and share bathrooms, classrooms, and frequently touched surfaces. CDC figures also show norovirus causes 58% of foodborne illnesses in the U.S. each year, and about 21 million Americans are diagnosed annually. Even without severe outcomes such as hospitalization, a cluster of vomiting and diarrhea cases can quickly affect attendance, caregiving, and household exposure, especially when family members also get sick. National CDC data show medium norovirus activity, without major spikes. So while the Kansas outbreak does not point to a nationwide surge, localized outbreaks can still happen when the virus reaches the right setting. What can be done? In Olathe, the response depended on coordination between public health officials and school leaders. The Johnson County Department of Health and Environment and Olathe Public Schools monitored illnesses, shared public health guidance, and worked to limit additional spread while the outbreak was active. For individual families, the guidance is simple: Wash hands with soap and water. CDC guidance says that is the most effective way to prevent norovirus from spreading and that hand sanitizer does not kill norovirus. Recovery usually happens within one to three days, but people can keep spreading the virus for several days after that, so improving symptoms do not necessarily mean the risk has ended at home or at school. Parents and staff should watch for nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, and diarrhea. Fever, headaches, and body aches can also occur. "Throughout the outbreak, JCDHE worked closely with school officials to monitor illnesses, provide public health guidance and help prevent further spread," the school district and health department said in a joint statement. "Although the outbreak is considered over, JCDHE and the Olathe Public Schools will continue to monitor the situation and work together to help protect the health of students, staff and families." Where can I learn more? For more on how health risks can spread in schools and other shared spaces, these stories add context. • At UConn, officials called it a considerable concern as tick-borne illnesses spread on campus. • In schools, air quality in classrooms is raising concerns about children's exposure. • In Mobile County, Alabama, a deadly virus detected prompted officials to warn travelers. She joined the brand in 2022. People Editorial Guidelines Published on October 23, 2026 11:37AM EDT 7 Comments Add Us On Bentwood Elementary School in Olathe, Kansas (stock image). Credit : Google Maps NEED TO KNOW Nearly 100 students and staff have been linked to a norovirus outbreak at Bentwood Elementary School in Olathe, Kansas Health officials said no hospitalizations were reported and no new cases were reported as of Oct. 13 Norovirus spreads easily through contaminated food surfaces and close contact, making handwashing especially important, the CDC said A norovirus outbreak has affected nearly 100 people at an elementary school in Kansas. There were 95 cases reported among students and staff linked to an outbreak at the Bentwood Elementary School in Olathe, Kansas, a joint statement from Johnson County Department of Health and Environment (JCDHE) and Olathe Public Schools obtained by PEOPLE read. Two more cases were reported among family members outside the school, according to JCDHE Director Charlie Hunt, per KCTV. Norovirus is a highly contagious virus that causes vomiting and diarrhea, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The agency said the virus spreads “very easily” through contaminated food or liquids, direct contact with an infected person, or touching contaminated objects and surfaces. Symptoms reported by people impacted by the outbreak included vomiting, diarrhea, nausea and stomach pain, per the joint statement. A micrograph of the norovirus (stock image). BSIP/UIG Via Getty Two of the norovirus cases reported at the elementary school were confirmed through laboratory testing, while the remaining cases were considered “epidemiologically linked,” meaning those affected experienced similar symptoms around the same time and in the same setting, suggesting they were part of the same outbreak. “Bentwood Elementary first experienced student absences involving similar illness symptoms on October 8,” per the statement. Never miss a story — sign up for PEOPLE’s free daily newsletter to stay up-to-date on the best of what PEOPLE has to offer, from celebrity news to compelling human interest stories. There were no hospitalizations reported during the outbreak, which reportedly occurred during the beginning of October. As of Oct. 13, there had been no new cases reported. The JCDHE confirmed in a social media post on Wednesday, Oct. 21, that the norovirus outbreak at the school was “over.” “Throughout the outbreak, JCDHE worked closely with school officials to monitor illnesses, provide public health guidance and help prevent further spread,” the school district and health department continued in their joint statement. Related Stories Cruise Passengers Hit with Norovirus as Ship Experiences Second Outbreak in a Month Foodborne Parasitic Outbreak That Causes 'Explosive' Diarrhea Has Spread to 17 States “Although the outbreak is considered over, JCDHE and the Olathe Public Schools will continue to monitor the situation and work together to help protect the health of students, staff and families,” they added. Dr. Dana Hawkinson, an infectious disease physician and medical director of infection prevention and control at the University of Kansas Health System, told KCTV that outbreaks like these can be very common. VIPs Get More The PEOPLE stories you love, with first access and special features reserved for subscribers. Subscribe Now “It’s very common to see outbreaks or clusters because this virus, when it is shed, again, through the fecal route, is very easy to contaminate places. So it is very important to wash your hands with soap and water to help decrease the contamination around,” Hawkinson said. “But those viruses are very small. And so you don’t know and understand when you have contact with them, especially if you’re in a household.” According to JCDHE Director Hunt, per KCTV, the number of cases was likely higher because of how contagious norovirus is. Never miss a story — sign up for PEOPLE’s free daily newsletter to stay up-to-date on the best of what PEOPLE has to offer, from celebrity news to compelling human interest stories. The CDC said norovirus is the leading cause of foodborne illness in the U.S., and causes 58% of foodborne illnesses acquired in the U.S. It is responsible for nearly 1 million pediatric medical care visits annually and it causes 19 to 21 million illnesses on average each year. news.content_title: Nearly 100 Students Fall Ill After Norovirus Outbreak Hits Elementary School
news.content: Almost 100 students and staff at a Kansas elementary school have fallen ill after a norovirus outbreak ravaged the campus. Almost 100 students and staff at a Kansas elementary school have fallen ill after a norovirus outbreak ravaged the campus. Videos by Wide Open Country Powered By 00:00/01:28 10 Sec Taylor Swift reveals her 'tools' to help her deal with the 'chaos' of fame Next Stay Indeed, Bentwood Elementary School in Olathe, Kansas, had 95 incidents of students and staff getting sick linked to the virus, according to PEOPLE, citing a joint statement from the Johnson County Department of Health and Environment (JCDHE) and Olathe Public Schools. Furthermore, it appears the norovirus outbreak spread beyond the elementary school. Per local outlet KCTV, 2 family members outside the school have come down with norovirus, too. According to the Cleveland Clinic, typical symptoms of norovirus include vomiting, diarrhea, and nausea. Victims of the highly contagious virus may also experience body aches, stomach distress, a headache, or a fever. It's normally spread through contaminated food or through contact with those carrying the virus. Norovirus usually runs its course in about one to three days, according to the outlet. Two of the cases at the elementary school were confirmed via laboratory testing. Meanwhile, other cases were declared "epidemiologically linked," meaning experts consider the symptoms of those ill to be directly related. "Bentwood Elementary first experienced student absences involving similar illness symptoms on October 8," the agencies' statement added, per PEOPLE. Officials Believe They're Clear of the Elementary School Norovirus Outbreak So far, no hospitalizations have been reported in connection with the norovirus outbreak. Since Oct. 13, no new cases stemming from the outbreak have been reported. By Oct. 21, officials declared the concerning health crisis over. "Throughout the outbreak, JCDHE worked closely with school officials to monitor illnesses, provide public health guidance, and help prevent further spread," the school district and health department explained in their joint statement. "Although the outbreak is considered over, JCDHE and the Olathe Public Schools will continue to monitor the situation and work together to help protect the health of students, staff, and families," the agencies pointed out. Meanwhile, infectious disease physician and medical director of infection prevention and control at the University of Kansas Health System, Dr. Dana Hawkinson, stressed that such outbreaks are common. "It's very common to see outbreaks or clusters because this virus, when it is shed, again, through the fecal route, is very easy to contaminate places. So it is very important to wash your hands with soap and water to help decrease the contamination around," Hawkinson explained to KCTV. "But those viruses are very small. And so you don't know and understand when you have contact with them, especially if you're in a household."

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Tuesday, October 27, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Norovirus infections in China linked to CNY 20.23 billion annual medical cost by October 26, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 Norovirus infections in China linked to CNY 20.23 billion annual medical cost Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Norovirus was detected in 18.80% of patients with acute gastroenteritis who underwent testing at medical institutions in four Chinese provinces between 2018 and 2024, according to a multicenter retrospective study that also estimated the infection’s national direct medical cost at CNY 20.23 billion per year. The analysis included 23,527 patients and combined hospital data with national population census and epidemiological survey information for the burden estimate. The findings show substantial variation in positivity, complications and medical spending by age and care setting, but the hospital-tested sample does not represent every acute gastroenteritis episode in China. The overall norovirus positivity rate was 18.80%, with a 95% confidence interval of 18.30% to 19.30%. Positivity was higher among inpatients, at 26.15% (95% CI 25.28% to 27.04%), than among outpatients, at 13.78% (95% CI 13.21% to 14.36%). Children younger than five years had the highest age-specific positivity rate, reaching 30.49% (95% CI 29.56% to 31.43%). Logistic regression models were used to analyze factors associated with norovirus infection, hospitalization risk, complications and direct medical costs, but the supplied results do not identify the individual predictors or report which ones were statistically significant. Among norovirus-positive patients, 18.97% (95% CI 17.84% to 20.16%) had at least one potential complication occurring concurrently with their acute gastroenteritis. Dehydration was the most prevalent, recorded in 11.28% of positive patients (95% CI 10.39% to 12.25%), followed by convulsions in 5.52% (95% CI 4.88% to 6.23%). The investigators described the clinical pattern as age-dependent: children younger than five tended to experience more severe manifestations, while patients aged 65 or older appeared to bear higher direct medical expenditure in the hospital-based sample. These were observational findings and do not establish that age itself caused differences in infection, severity or spending. Median direct medical costs differed sharply between inpatient and outpatient care. The median cost for inpatients was CNY 4,580 per case, with an interquartile range of CNY 3,129 to CNY 6,402, compared with CNY 230 for outpatients, with an interquartile range of CNY 128 to CNY 354. Adults aged 65 or older had the highest per-capita direct medical cost: a median of CNY 5,322, with an interquartile range of CNY 2,411 to CNY 10,798. At the national level, the model estimated that children younger than five bore an aggregate medical burden 11.2 times that of people aged 60 or older. The national annual direct medical cost of norovirus infection was estimated at CNY 20.23 billion by combining the multicenter study with national population census and epidemiological survey data. The estimate is subject to the representativeness of institutions in four provinces, the selection of patients who received norovirus testing and the assumptions used to extend hospital-based observations nationwide. The study also concerned acute gastroenteritis patients seeking medical consultation, and its age, regional and seasonal comparisons should not be interpreted as population-wide trends over time. Within these limits, the results identify a heterogeneous burden: high positivity and more severe clinical manifestations among young children, higher per-patient expenditure among older adults and a substantial cost associated with hospital care. The authors concluded that age-targeted public health strategies and regionally tailored allocation of healthcare resources are needed to address these differences. The analysis included 23,527 patients and combined hospital data with national population census and epidemiological survey information for the burden estimate. The findings show substantial variation in positivity, complications and medical spending by age and care setting, but the hospital-tested sample does not represent every acute gastroenteritis episode in China. The overall norovirus positivity rate was 18.80%, with a 95% confidence interval of 18.30% to 19.30%. Positivity was higher among inpatients, at 26.15% (95% CI 25.28% to 27.04%), than among outpatients, at 13.78% (95% CI 13.21% to 14.36%). Children younger than five years had the highest age-specific positivity rate, reaching 30.49% (95% CI 29.56% to 31.43%). Logistic regression models were used to analyze factors associated with norovirus infection, hospitalization risk, complications and direct medical costs, but the supplied results do not identify the individual predictors or report which ones were statistically significant. Among norovirus-positive patients, 18.97% (95% CI 17.84% to 20.16%) had at least one potential complication occurring concurrently with their acute gastroenteritis. Dehydration was the most prevalent, recorded in 11.28% of positive patients (95% CI 10.39% to 12.25%), followed by convulsions in 5.52% (95% CI 4.88% to 6.23%). The investigators described the clinical pattern as age-dependent: children younger than five tended to experience more severe manifestations, while patients aged 65 or older appeared to bear higher direct medical expenditure in the hospital-based sample. These were observational findings and do not establish that age itself caused differences in infection, severity or spending. Median direct medical costs differed sharply between inpatient and outpatient care. The median cost for inpatients was CNY 4,580 per case, with an interquartile range of CNY 3,129 to CNY 6,402, compared with CNY 230 for outpatients, with an interquartile range of CNY 128 to CNY 354. Adults aged 65 or older had the highest per-capita direct medical cost: a median of CNY 5,322, with an interquartile range of CNY 2,411 to CNY 10,798. At the national level, the model estimated that children younger than five bore an aggregate medical burden 11.2 times that of people aged 60 or older. The national annual direct medical cost of norovirus infection was estimated at CNY 20.23 billion by combining the multicenter study with national population census and epidemiological survey data. The estimate is subject to the representativeness of institutions in four provinces, the selection of patients who received norovirus testing and the assumptions used to extend hospital-based observations nationwide. The study also concerned acute gastroenteritis patients seeking medical consultation, and its age, regional and seasonal comparisons should not be interpreted as population-wide trends over time. Within these limits, the results identify a heterogeneous burden: high positivity and more severe clinical manifestations among young children, higher per-patient expenditure among older adults and a substantial cost associated with hospital care. The authors concluded that age-targeted public health strategies and regionally tailored allocation of healthcare resources are needed to address these differences. She joined the brand in 2022. People Editorial Guidelines Published on October 23, 2026 11:37AM EDT 7 Comments Add Us On Bentwood Elementary School in Olathe, Kansas (stock image). Credit : Google Maps NEED TO KNOW Nearly 100 students and staff have been linked to a norovirus outbreak at Bentwood Elementary School in Olathe, Kansas Health officials said no hospitalizations were reported and no new cases were reported as of Oct. 13 Norovirus spreads easily through contaminated food surfaces and close contact, making handwashing especially important, the CDC said A norovirus outbreak has affected nearly 100 people at an elementary school in Kansas. There were 95 cases reported among students and staff linked to an outbreak at the Bentwood Elementary School in Olathe, Kansas, a joint statement from Johnson County Department of Health and Environment (JCDHE) and Olathe Public Schools obtained by PEOPLE read. Two more cases were reported among family members outside the school, according to JCDHE Director Charlie Hunt, per KCTV. Norovirus is a highly contagious virus that causes vomiting and diarrhea, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The agency said the virus spreads “very easily” through contaminated food or liquids, direct contact with an infected person, or touching contaminated objects and surfaces. Symptoms reported by people impacted by the outbreak included vomiting, diarrhea, nausea and stomach pain, per the joint statement. A micrograph of the norovirus (stock image). BSIP/UIG Via Getty Two of the norovirus cases reported at the elementary school were confirmed through laboratory testing, while the remaining cases were considered “epidemiologically linked,” meaning those affected experienced similar symptoms around the same time and in the same setting, suggesting they were part of the same outbreak. “Bentwood Elementary first experienced student absences involving similar illness symptoms on October 8,” per the statement. Never miss a story — sign up for PEOPLE’s free daily newsletter to stay up-to-date on the best of what PEOPLE has to offer, from celebrity news to compelling human interest stories. There were no hospitalizations reported during the outbreak, which reportedly occurred during the beginning of October. As of Oct. 13, there had been no new cases reported. The JCDHE confirmed in a social media post on Wednesday, Oct. 21, that the norovirus outbreak at the school was “over.” “Throughout the outbreak, JCDHE worked closely with school officials to monitor illnesses, provide public health guidance and help prevent further spread,” the school district and health department continued in their joint statement. Related Stories Cruise Passengers Hit with Norovirus as Ship Experiences Second Outbreak in a Month Foodborne Parasitic Outbreak That Causes 'Explosive' Diarrhea Has Spread to 17 States “Although the outbreak is considered over, JCDHE and the Olathe Public Schools will continue to monitor the situation and work together to help protect the health of students, staff and families,” they added. Dr. Dana Hawkinson, an infectious disease physician and medical director of infection prevention and control at the University of Kansas Health System, told KCTV that outbreaks like these can be very common. VIPs Get More The PEOPLE stories you love, with first access and special features reserved for subscribers. Subscribe Now “It’s very common to see outbreaks or clusters because this virus, when it is shed, again, through the fecal route, is very easy to contaminate places. So it is very important to wash your hands with soap and water to help decrease the contamination around,” Hawkinson said. “But those viruses are very small. And so you don’t know and understand when you have contact with them, especially if you’re in a household.” According to JCDHE Director Hunt, per KCTV, the number of cases was likely higher because of how contagious norovirus is. Never miss a story — sign up for PEOPLE’s free daily newsletter to stay up-to-date on the best of what PEOPLE has to offer, from celebrity news to compelling human interest stories. The CDC said norovirus is the leading cause of foodborne illness in the U.S., and causes 58% of foodborne illnesses acquired in the U.S. It is responsible for nearly 1 million pediatric medical care visits annually and it causes 19 to 21 million illnesses on average each year. supplementary_news.content: Norovirus Risk Extends Beyond Oysters, with Leafy Greens Linked to 32% of Foodborne Cases by Kim Bo Mi Updated 2026/10/27 13:06 Norovirus can also be contracted through vegetables. /AI-generated photo Norovirus infections surge from November, when the weather turns cold. Oysters are a ëíì ì ̧ food ingredient that raises the risk of infection, but people can also contract norovirus through vegetables. Norovirus can survive even at minus 20Â°C. It can enter the body through contaminated ingredients, including seafood as well as fruits and vegetables. In particular, vegetables stored in the refrigerator should not be eaten without washing them. An investigation by the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, CDC, into foods linked to norovirus outbreaks from 1998 to 2008 found that leafy greens accounted for the highest proportion, at 32%. Vegetables should be washed thoroughly before eating. /AI-generated photo When washing vegetables, soak them in water first and then rinse them thoroughly under running water. The MFDS analyzed the effectiveness of different washing methods in removing norovirus from lettuce and perilla leaves that had been artificially contaminated with the virus. The analysis found that soaking them in water for 2 minutes and then washing them under running water for 30 seconds removed 87.5% and 94.8% of the norovirus, respectively. When storing food, keep it in a separate container to prevent cross-contamination. Fruits and vegetables stored in the refrigerator after washing should also be washed again before eating. Food should preferably be heated to at least 85Â°C for 1 minute or longer before eating. Knives and cutting boards should be disinfected, and using separate cooking utensils for vegetables, meat and fish can lower the risk of infection. Wash your hands with soap under running water for at least 30 seconds before handling food. People infected with norovirus should be cautious about dehydration. Drinking boiled water with sugar and salt can help. /AI-generated photo People infected with norovirus develop symptoms of vomiting and diarrhea within 1 to 2 days. Abdominal pain, chills, fever, nausea and muscle aches can also occur. Most people recover naturally after 2 to 3 days, but caution is needed because dehydration can occur. If dehydration is severe, treatment involving intravenous fluid administration may be considered. When symptoms occur, drink plenty of fluids through sports drinks without caffeine or alcohol. The Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency said it is also helpful to drink boiled water mixed with four tablespoons of sugar and one tablespoon of salt per 1 L. Do not take antidiarrheal or antiemetic medication on your own without a doctor's examination. Once diarrhea symptoms improve, eat small amounts of thin rice porridge or rice gruel. If a family member has norovirus, separate the person's living space from the rest of the household. Disinfect items the patient has touched or used with a mixture of bleach and water in a ratio of 1 to 50. Clothes should preferably be sanitized by washing them at 70Â°C or higher. To be safe, the patient should not prepare food for 3 days after recovering. This article has been translated AI. by Kim Bo Mi View All Articles Copyright Â© Health Chosun. supplementary_news.content: Topics Business & Management Carpet Facility Management Hard Floors Health & Safety Infection Control Products Restrooms Technology & Trends Training Follow CMM Facebook X LinkedIn Get Your CMM Magazine Subscription Sign up for the CMM Newsletter Advertise with Us Join ISSA News Magazine Resources Certifications / Standards Safer Choices Product Innovation Showcase Sponsored Content Education Videos Industry Research On-Demand Webinars Follow CMM Facebook X LinkedIn Get Your CMM Magazine Subscription Sign up for the CMM Newsletter Advertise with Us Join ISSA Events ISSA Show Industry Events Upcoming Webinars Follow CMM Facebook X LinkedIn Get Your CMM Magazine Subscription Sign up for the CMM Newsletter Advertise with Us Join ISSA ISSA Media Follow CMM Facebook X LinkedIn Get Your CMM Magazine Subscription Sign up for the CMM Newsletter Advertise with Us Join ISSA Contact Subscribe ADVERTISE Nearly 100 Cases of Norovirus Reported at One Kansas School Norovirus cases are at medium levels nationally October 27, 2026 A Kansas elementary school experienced a norovirus outbreak that affected nearly 100 people, Johnson County Health officials said. The outbreak at Bentwood Elementary School in Olathe, Kansas, began in early October and spread to 95 cases among students and staff and two among family members in the Kansas City metropolitan area. Two of the cases were confirmed through laboratory testing, and the remaining cases were “epidemiologically linked, meaning individuals experienced similar symptoms around the same time and in the same setting,” officials said. Norovirus is the leading cause of vomiting, diarrhea and foodborne illness in the United States, and people of all ages can get infected and sick with norovirus, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. According to school and county health officials, people impacted by the outbreak at Bentwood Elementary experienced symptoms including vomiting, diarrhea, nausea and stomach pain. Officials said no hospitalizations were reported, and no new cases have been reported since Oct. 13. Throughout the outbreak, the local health department has worked closely with school officials to monitor illnesses, provide public health guidance and help prevent further spread. While the outbreak is considered over, local teams will continue to monitor the situation. Annually, around 21 million Americans are diagnosed with norovirus. The virus is incredibly contagious and frequently reported in school settings, where children interact in close quarters. The CDC said the most effective way to prevent norovirus spread is washing hands with soap and water. Hand sanitizer does not kill norovirus. Current CDC data shows that norovirus cases are at medium levels nationally, without significant spikes. Tags U.S. Green Building Council Streamlines Zero Waste Certification October 27, 2026 Last week, the U.S. Green Building Council (USGBC) launched TRUE v2—the next iteration of the TRUE (Total Resource Use and Efficiency) zero waste certification program. The new version of the rating system emphasizes zero waste impacts and global applicability, and it helps organizations advance their decarbonization, business transformation and circularity goals. For more than 10 years, TRUE has reshaped waste operations for organizations, companies and small businesses, with over 680 certified projects totaling 272 million square feet and diverting 8.9 million tons of waste from landfills. The streamlined rating system collects, measures, benchmarks and verifies sustainability performance. Updates to the TRUE v2 rating system include: Rebalanced credit structure to support projects starting their zero-waste journey while also rewarding high performers. Improved global usability with clearer, internationally applicable language and approaches. Greater rewards for higher-impact and harder-to-achieve actions. TRUE v2 comes as more organizations seek clarity on zero waste roadmaps, with waste volumes rising, landfill capacity tightening, and disposal costs escalating. The Global Waste Management Outlook 2024 projects that the direct cost of waste management could double by 2050, and the Environmental Research and Education Foundation found that commercial waste disposal costs in the U.S. have grown by 15-30% since 2016. TRUE v2 was developed with USGBC members and stakeholders, including the TRUE Advisory Council, and informed by global public consultation from zero waste practitioners. Registration for TRUE v2 is now open on the Arc platform for projects interested in advancing their zero waste goals and pursuing certification.
